basic_details.scholarship_name: Norwegian Directorate (HK-dir) / NORPART Postgraduate Research Grants
basic_details.offering_entity: Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (Direktoratet for høyere utdanning og kompetanse - HK-dir) & Norwegian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
basic_details.host_institutions_covered: Accredited Norwegian public universities (e.g., Norwegian University of Science and Technology - NTNU, University of Oslo - UiO, University of Bergen - UiB, Norwegian University of Life Sciences - NMBU, UiT The Arctic University of Norway)
basic_details.major_restrictions: Prioritized institutional partnership domains: Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Renewable Energy & Power Systems, Environmental & Climate Sciences, Marine Informatics, Biotechnology, and Global Health.
basic_details.number_of_awards_total: ~100 to 150 bilateral mobility and postgraduate degree grants awarded annually across international partner consortia
basic_details.number_of_awards_pakistan: Allocated across formal Pakistani university partnerships (e.g., NUST, COMSATS, Quaid-i-Azam University); ~8 to 15 Pakistani researchers awarded annually
basic_details.duration_of_scholarship: Up to 2 years for Master of Science; up to 3-4 years for PhD research fellowship positions

nationality_requirements: Citizens of designated partner countries holding institutional collaborations with Norway (Pakistan fully eligible)
eligibility_requirements.age_limit_notes: No statutory age limit; candidates are evaluated based on academic merit, research competence, and departmental nomination.
eligibility_requirements.academic_qualifications: A recognized 4-year Bachelor of Science / Engineering (16 years education) with minimum CGPA 3.30 / 4.00 (or 75%+ aggregate) for Master's programs; an MS/MPhil (18 years education) with minimum CGPA 3.50 / 4.00 and thesis completion for PhD positions from an HEC-recognized university in Pakistan.
eligibility_requirements.grading_conversion_notes: Norwegian grading system uses A to F (A highest, E lowest passing). Applicants typically require an equivalent of Grade B or Grade A on the Norwegian scale.
eligibility_requirements.subject_background_prerequisites: Rigorous undergraduate background in relevant engineering, mathematical, or scientific discipline with minimum 80 ECTS of specialized subject coursework.
eligibility_requirements.current_education_status: Graduating seniors in their final semester or enrolled Master's/PhD scholars at Pakistani partner institutions.
eligibility_requirements.work_experience_notes: Prior academic publications, laboratory research, or thesis projects are highly advantageous for PhD and Master's fellowship candidates.
eligibility_requirements.language_notes: IELTS Academic minimum 6.5 overall (no band below 6.0) or TOEFL iBT minimum 90. Certain partner projects accept institutional Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificates from Pakistani partner universities with English-medium curricula.
eligibility_requirements.other_language_requirements: None; academic instruction and thesis supervision are conducted entirely in English.
eligibility_requirements.special_eligibility_categories: Applicants must be nominated or enrolled through an approved institutional partnership agreement between a Norwegian host university and a Pakistani partner university.
eligibility_requirements.previous_scholarship_restrictions: Cannot hold another Norwegian government grant simultaneously.

tuition_fee.details: Full exemption/grant coverage for tuition fees at Norwegian public universities (which instituted tuition fees for non-EEA students in autumn 2023; HK-dir partner fellows are granted complete institutional tuition waivers or direct project fee subsidies).

admission_application_fee.details: Norwegian public universities do not charge an admission application fee.

accommodation.details: Guaranteed priority placement in university student housing (SiO in Oslo, SiT in Trondheim, Sammen in Bergen); rent is paid via the monthly living stipend.

monthly_stipend.details: Monthly tax-free living stipend aligned with the Norwegian State Educational Loan Fund (Lånekassen) subsistence benchmark of NOK 11,500 to NOK 13,790 per month (~PKR 300,000 - 360,000 / month). For employed PhD research fellows, full salary on the state pay scale (approx NOK 532,000 / year before tax).

airfare.details: Fixed round-trip travel grant covering economy flights between Pakistan and Norway at the start and conclusion of the study period.

visa_fee.details: Norwegian Directorate of Immigration (UDI) residence permit application fee for studies (NOK 5,900) is reimbursed or waived under institutional grant agreements.

health_insurance.details: Automatic enrollment in the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme (Folketrygden) upon registration and receiving a Norwegian National Identity Number (Fødselsnummer), providing comprehensive universal public healthcare.

food_allowance.details: Covered via the monthly living stipend of NOK 11,500 - 13,790.

books_and_materials_allowance.details: Study materials and laboratory equipment are covered under project operational allocations; computer lab and campus infrastructure access provided.

research_funding_conference_grant.details: Generous project budget for research travel, field work, and attending international conferences across Europe and North America.
research_funding_conference_grant.amount: Up to NOK 25,000 / year for approved research activities

travel_transit_allowance.details: Comprehensive round-trip airfare and local airport transit grant provided.

university_and_program_options.single_or_multiple_universities: Multiple accredited Norwegian public research universities participating in HK-dir partnership consortia.
participating_institutions: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU Trondheim)
Norwegian University of Life Sciences (NMBU Ås)
UiT The Arctic University of Norway (Tromsø)
university_and_program_options.university_rankings_scope: NTNU and University of Oslo consistently rank within the top 100-150 globally (QS/THE World University Rankings), with world-renowned standing in computer engineering, clean tech, and earth sciences.
university_and_program_options.program_duration: 2 years (120 ECTS) for Master of Science; 3 to 4 years for Doctor of Philosophy
university_and_program_options.admission_requirements_summary: Relevant Bachelor's degree (180-240 ECTS equivalence) with top-quartile grades, certified English proficiency, and institutional endorsement from the Pakistani partner university.
university_and_program_options.easiest_hardest_institutions_guidance: NTNU Computer Science and UiO Informatics are highly competitive, requiring strong theoretical foundations and programming competence; NMBU and UiT offer specialized niches with high fellowship allocation rates for environmental and data science projects.
university_and_program_options.strategic_program_match_advice: Check whether your home department in Pakistan (e.g. at NUST, QAU, or COMSATS) maintains active HK-dir/NORPART or UTFORSK project partnerships with NTNU or UiO; direct faculty-to-faculty recommendation is the most reliable pathway to winning this award.

application_process_roadmap.account_creation_instructions: Register on Søknadsweb for the targeted Norwegian university, submit academic profile, and coordinate with the Pakistani partner department coordinator for bilateral project nomination.
step_by_step_workflow: Step 1: Identify participating HK-dir/NORPART project coordinators at Pakistani partner university and Norwegian host university.
Step 2: Submit formal departmental nomination and academic portfolio to the institutional project coordinator.
Step 3: Complete university admission application through Søknadsweb (official Norwegian university admissions portal) by December 1.
Step 4: Upload attested transcripts, degree certificates, CV, statement of purpose, and English language test scores.
Step 5: Attend academic screening interview if shortlisted by the project evaluation committee.
Step 6: Receive formal admission letter and HK-dir scholarship commitment letter; apply for UDI student residence permit.
application_process_roadmap.university_vs_scholarship_routing: Integrated Bilateral Track: Candidates are nominated via the inter-university partnership agreement and apply through Søknadsweb in parallel.
application_process_roadmap.recommendation_letters_submission_method: Submitted by academic referees directly to the project coordinator or uploaded via Søknadsweb.
application_process_roadmap.personal_statement_prompts: Statement of purpose outlining research interests, academic background, and relevance to the bilateral Norway-Pakistan project.
application_process_roadmap.study_plan_research_proposal_requirement: Structured research proposal (2-4 pages) aligned with the research themes of the HK-dir/NORPART project.
application_process_roadmap.cv_format_requirements: Academic CV highlighting publications, software repositories, and research project experience.
application_process_roadmap.interview_format_details: 30-40 minute technical discussion via Microsoft Teams / Zoom assessing academic depth and research motivation.
application_process_roadmap.standardized_tests: IELTS Academic (min 6.5 overall, 6.0 each band) or TOEFL iBT (min 90); MOI accepted by select consortia.
application_process_roadmap.application_fee_amount: NOK 0 (Free of charge at Norwegian public universities)
application_process_roadmap.attestation_requirements: Degrees and transcripts attested by HEC Pakistan and MOFA; Matric/Inter attested by IBCC.
application_process_roadmap.translation_requirements: Certified English translation required for all official documents.
application_process_roadmap.final_submission_method: Online submission via Søknadsweb portal and bilateral departmental nomination dossier.

required_documents_checklist.document_name: Official Academic Transcripts and Degree Certificates
required_documents_checklist.specification: Complete transcripts for 16-year Bachelor's (for MSc) or 18-year MS/MPhil (for PhD) with Grade B / CGPA 3.3+ equivalent.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Scans of HEC-attested degrees and semester transcripts.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Official letter from Pakistani partner university endorsing the candidate under the HK-dir/NORPART partnership.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Signed by Dean or Head of Department at partner Pakistani university.

required_documents_checklist.specification: 2 to 4-page proposal detailing research objectives, methodology, and relevance to bilateral project.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Must clearly cite the host Norwegian research lab and faculty mentors.

required_documents_checklist.specification: IELTS Academic (min 6.5) or TOEFL iBT (min 90), or approved MOI certificate.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Scores must be valid at time of application.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Confidential recommendation letters from previous academic professors or research supervisors.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Must be on university letterhead with institutional email addresses.

required_documents_checklist.specification: Clear color copy of passport identification page with minimum 2-year validity.
required_documents_checklist.pakistan_specific_instruction: Pakistani passport must remain valid through mid-2028.

important_dates_timeline.annual_cycle_notes: Main intake cycle is Autumn (August commencement). December 1 deadline is strictly enforced on Søknadsweb.

selection_process_and_weights.research_experience_weight: 30% (Prior research, thesis publications, and proposal alignment)
selection_process_and_weights.personal_statement_weight: 10% (Clarity of purpose and bilateral collaboration potential)
selection_process_and_weights.interview_weight: 0% (Interview performance factored directly into research proposal score)
selection_process_and_weights.financial_need_weight: 0% (Pure academic and bilateral research merit evaluation)
selection_process_and_weights.selection_panel_composition: Joint evaluation committee of Norwegian host faculty, Pakistani partner department, and HK-dir academic officers.
selection_process_and_weights.evaluation_methodology: Two-tier review: departmental nomination followed by joint faculty evaluation on Søknadsweb.

competitiveness_profile.acceptance_rate_pakistan: ~10% to 15% among officially nominated partner candidates
competitiveness_profile.typical_successful_applicant_gpa: CGPA 3.50+ / 4.00 or top 10% class rank from top Pakistani universities (NUST, QAU, COMSATS, UET)
competitiveness_profile.typical_academic_and_research_profile: High-performing STEM graduates with strong mathematical foundations, thesis research experience, and supervisor connections.
competitiveness_profile.common_backgrounds_of_winners: Graduates of partner engineering and science faculties in Pakistan.
competitiveness_profile.high_representation_countries: Pakistan, India, South Africa, Tanzania, Ethiopia, Brazil, Nepal, Vietnam.

fake_websites_and_scams: Beware of fraudulent consultancy firms advertising 'Norwegian free visa & work permits'.
Official Norwegian applications are submitted exclusively via Søknadsweb and university portals.
red_flags_and_warnings.application_fee_warning: Norwegian public universities do NOT charge any admission application fee.
red_flags_and_warnings.agent_and_intermediary_warnings: HK-dir and Norwegian public universities do not work with educational agents.
hidden_costs_breakdown: UDI study residence permit fee: NOK 5,900 (~PKR 155,000) payable upfront, reimbursed later.
VFS Global appointment and biometric fee in Pakistan: ~PKR 15,000.
Tuberculosis screening test at IOM Islamabad/Lahore: ~PKR 18,000.
Initial pocket money before first stipend transfer in Norway: ~NOK 5,000 (~PKR 130,000).
misleading_claims_debunked: Myth: Norway abolished all free education for international students so no one gets funded. Reality: While general tuition was introduced in 2023, HK-dir, NORPART, and bilateral fellowship holders receive 100% full tuition coverage and monthly stipends.
Myth: You can apply without an institutional partnership. Reality: NORPART grants are tied directly to active institutional inter-university agreements.
official_vs_unofficial_discrepancies: Unofficial sites claim Norway offers rolling admissions; Norwegian public university international deadlines close sharply on December 1.

scholarship_obligations_and_terms.minimum_gpa_maintenance: Must maintain Grade B or higher average across coursework and pass minimum 30 ECTS per semester.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.attendance_requirements: Full-time physical presence on campus in Norway and active laboratory/thesis research engagement.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.academic_progress_monitoring: Semester-end review of earned credits on the national student database (FS) and annual progress report by thesis advisor.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.work_restrictions_during_study: Part-time work permitted up to 20 hours per week during academic semesters, full-time during holidays.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.home_country_return_obligation: Depending on project agreement: mobility scholars return to home university; degree scholars may apply for 1-year Norwegian post-study job seeker visa.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.service_obligations_or_bonds: Participation in bilateral symposiums and reporting milestones to HK-dir project managers.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.repayment_clawback_conditions: Funding terminated upon voluntary withdrawal or severe academic negligence without approved cause.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_university: Non-transferable to other universities; tied specifically to the partner consortium.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.rules_for_changing_major: Strictly prohibited; fellowship is allocated to the designated research project.
scholarship_obligations_and_terms.extension_policy: Maximum extension of one semester considered for legitimate medical or research delays with project lead approval.
